text: Here's a puzzle. A neural network watches a person walk, and predicts what a radar will see.
say: Here's a puzzle. A neural network watches a person walk, and predicts what a radar will see.
heard: Here's a puzzle. A neural network watches a person walk and predicts what a radar will see.

text: It's accurate. Really accurate. But did it learn the physics, or did it just get good at guessing?
say: It's accurate. Really accurate. But did it learn the physics, or did it just get good at guessing?
heard: It's accurate, really accurate. But did it learn the physics, or did it just get good at guessing?

text: Today: a paper that found a way to check.
say: Today: a paper that found a way to check.
heard: Today, a paper that found a way to check.

text: Welcome to the aigs pod. This is a short pilot for our journal club. The voice you're hearing is synthetic, generated on a laptop.
say: Welcome to the [aigs](/ˈAɡz/) pod. This is a short pilot for our journal club. The voice you're hearing is synthetic, generated on a laptop.
heard: Welcome to the AgsPod. This is a short pilot for our journal club. The voice you're hearing is synthetic, generated on a laptop.

text: The paper is called LAWFUL, by Kevin Chen, Kenneth Parker, and Anish Arora, from the mechanistic interpretability workshop at ICML.
say: The paper is called LAWFUL, by Kevin Chen, Kenneth Parker, and Anish Arora, from the mechanistic interpretability workshop at ICML.
heard: The paper is called Lawful, by Kevin Chen, Kenneth Parker, and Anish Arora, from the Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop at ICML.

text: First, the setup. The model takes in motion capture: fifty-three markers on a moving body, frame after frame.
say: First, the setup. The model takes in motion capture: fifty-three markers on a moving body, frame after frame.
heard: First, the setup. The model takes in motion capture, 53 markers on a moving body, frame after frame.

text: And it predicts a radar spectrogram. Think of it as a picture of how fast each part of the body is moving toward or away from the radar, over time.
say: And it predicts a radar spectrogram. Think of it as a picture of how fast each part of the body is moving toward or away from the radar, over time.
heard: And it predicts a radar spectrogram. Think of it as a picture of how fast each part of the body is moving toward or away from the radar over time.

text: Radar obeys a simple law, the Doppler law. The frequency shift is twice the speed toward the radar, divided by the wavelength.
say: Radar obeys a simple law, the Doppler law. The frequency shift is twice the speed toward the radar, divided by the wavelength.
heard: Radar obeys a simple law, the Doppler law. The frequency shift is twice the speed toward the radar, divided by the wavelength.

text: Here's the catch. The model was never shown a single velocity. Only positions in, and radar out.
say: Here's the catch. The model was never shown a single velocity. Only positions in, and radar out.
heard: Here's the catch. The model was never shown a single velocity, only positions in and radar out.

text: So if it predicts the radar correctly, somewhere inside, it has to turn positions into speed. Does it?
say: So if it predicts the radar correctly, somewhere inside, it has to turn positions into speed. Does it?
heard: So if it predicts the radar correctly, somewhere inside, it has to turn positions into speed, does it?

text: The paper checks in three steps: behavior, cause, and mechanism.
say: The paper checks in three steps: behavior, cause, and mechanism.
heard: The paper checks in three steps, behavior, cause, and mechanism.

text: Behavior first. Imagine taking a recording of someone walking, and replaying it with every movement toward the radar slowed to thirty percent. The sideways motion stays the same.
say: Behavior first. Imagine taking a recording of someone walking, and replaying it with every movement toward the radar slowed to thirty percent. The sideways motion stays the same.
heard: Behavior first. Imagine taking a recording of someone walking and replaying it with every movement toward the radar slowed to 30%. The sideways motion stays the same.

text: Physics tells you exactly what should happen: the Doppler shift should shrink to thirty percent too.
say: Physics tells you exactly what should happen: the Doppler shift should shrink to thirty percent too.
heard: Physics tells you exactly what should happen. The Doppler shift should shrink to 30% too.

text: These what-if inputs are called counterfactuals. Run lots of them, from fast, to frozen, to reversed, and compare the model's response with the law's.
say: These what-if inputs are called counterfactuals. Run lots of them, from fast, to frozen, to reversed, and compare the model's response with the law's.
heard: These what-if inputs are called counterfactuals. Run lots of them from fast to frozen to reversed and compare the model's response with the laws.

text: Within the speeds this radar can actually measure, the agreement score is zero point nine eight eight, where one is perfect. The behavior follows the law.
say: Within the speeds this radar can actually measure, the agreement score is zero point nine eight eight, where one is perfect. The behavior follows the law.
heard: Within the speeds this radar can actually measure, the agreement score is 0.988, where one is perfect. The behavior follows the law.

text: Step two, cause. Which parts of the network produce that behavior?
say: Step two, cause. Which parts of the network produce that behavior?
heard: Step 2, cause. Which parts of the network produce that behavior?

text: The tool is activation patching. You copy what a few components compute on the what-if input into the original run, and see whether the output follows.
say: The tool is activation patching. You copy what a few components compute on the what-if input into the original run, and see whether the output follows.
heard: The tool is activation patching. You copy what a few components compute on the what-if input into the original run and see whether the output follows.

text: A search grows that set of components, piece by piece. About half of them recover ninety-one percent of the agreement, and nearly all sit in the part of the model that looks across time.
say: A search grows that set of components, piece by piece. About half of them recover ninety-one percent of the agreement, and nearly all sit in the part of the model that looks across time.
heard: A search grows that set of components, piece by piece. About half of them recover 91% of the agreement, and nearly all sit in the part of the model that looks across time.

text: Step three, mechanism. How do those parts compute speed?
say: Step three, mechanism. How do those parts compute speed?
heard: Step 3, Mechanism. How do those parts compute speed?

text: Two attention heads give it away. One looks at the earliest frames. The other looks at the latest.
say: Two attention heads give it away. One looks at the earliest frames. The other looks at the latest.
heard: Two attention heads give it away. One looks at the earliest frames, the other looks at the latest.

text: And velocity is exactly that: where you are late, minus where you were early.
say: And velocity is exactly that: where you are late, minus where you were early.
heard: And velocity is exactly that, where you are late minus where you were early.

text: Some things to bring to the meeting.

text: Is one number, the average Doppler shift, enough to say the model uses the law?
say: Is one number, the average Doppler shift, enough to say the model uses the law?

text: Outside the radar's range, the agreement breaks down. Is that physics, or just data the model never saw?
say: Outside the radar's range, the agreement breaks down. Is that physics, or just data the model never saw?

text: And the big one: what would this method need, for a law nobody knows in advance?
